digest.component_or_area: review-bot Bedrock IAM grant on rebar-gerrit-instance-role
propositions: The rebar-gerrit-instance-role lacks any Bedrock permission and must be granted scoped Bedrock access for the review-bot container via a new separately-owned inline policy, without modifying iam.tf.

The Converse API authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel (proven by a real from-instance call), not bedrock:Converse, so the grant must be InvokeModel + InvokeModelWithResponseStream scoped to Claude foundation models and inference profiles.

A policy simulator only reports what the named action permits, not which action the service actually checks, so scoped IAM grants must be verified by a real from-instance call plus a non-Claude negative control, never from a wildcard-holding identity.

IMDSv2 reachability from the review-bot container selects between an IAM-only path and a hop-limit contingency (http_put_response_hop_limit=2); AC1 confirmed IMDS reachable so the contingency did not fire.
Region is unresolved inside the container (no AWS_REGION / bedrock-runtime raises NoRegionError) and is deliberately deferred to a separate cutover-prerequisite ticket, independent of the IAM grant.
Verification must confirm opcert SSM fetch and Gerrit startup still succeed after apply and that the container authenticates only as the instance role with no static AWS credential env vars.
